messages:
sarah: Quick heads-up — onboarding nova-lite-7B (converted from Gemma-style checkpoint) is showing odd generation diffs after int4 quant. Suspect rotary signature vs subtoken boundary mismatch; reproducer + logs below.

raj: Can you paste a tiny prompt + the divergent outputs? Also which conversion script did you use?

sarah: Example prompt: "Summarize: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
sarah: Gemma baseline (float32): "A short summary: A fast brown fox leaps over a sleepy dog."
sarah: Converted+int4 (nova-lite): "Summary: The quick brown jumps lazy."  <-- words dropped / garbled ordering.

sarah: Conversion cmd I used:```python tools/convert_checkpoint.py \ 
  --src gemma/checkpoint.pt \ 
  --dst nova-lite/converted.safetensors \ 
  --tokenizer gemma-tokenizer.json \ 
  --quant int4```

anya: Could be KV-cache misalignment or head-dim remap. We saw similar when headwise rotary params were shuffled. :eyes:

matt: Do you have token ids for the prompt and where the subtoken boundary is? Rotary rotations are head-dim dependent so an off-by-one in token mapping can produce that.

sarah: Tokenization for the prompt (gemma tokenizer): ```[101, 2027, 4248, 2123, 8731, 998, 198, 102]```
sarah: Tokenization when loaded by nova-lite tokenizer: ```[101, 2027, 4248, 2123, 8731, 998, 198, 102]```
sarah: Looks same for this short, but for longer examples we see a subtle subtoken split: e.g. 
sarah: gemma -> [345, 12, 789] 
    nova-lite -> [345, 1, 2, 789]  (so a boundary introduced)

raj: That smells like a normalization / unicode runes difference (NFKC vs NFC) or a pretokenizer whitespace handling change. Those extra subtokens shift rotary phase alignment when we index into KV cache.

ci-bot: Quick smoke bench results (this thread): 
  - ppl (eval set A): baseline 13.2 -> converted+int4 17.5 (+32%)
  - rouge-L on summarization sample: baseline 0.41 -> converted+int4 0.27
  - inference p95 latency: 85ms -> 82ms (ok)

kevin: Try the converter with the --preserve-rotary-order flag and also pass --tokenizer-normalize nfkc. Example:```python tools/convert_checkpoint.py --src ... --dst ... --quant int4 --preserve-rotary-order --tokenizer-normalize nfkc```

sarah: Ran with those flags, small improvement: ppl 15.1, rouge-L 0.33. Still not baseline but much closer.

matt: Another angle: int4 packing + kernel reorder can change the order of matmul ops vs fp32 path, exposing a bias when rotary wiring assumes predecessor head order. On our side we added a short unit test that forces round-trip of token ids through the tokenizer + rotary index mapping to ensure identity.

raj: Can you paste the rotary index mapping for both versions? Even a one-line diff would help.

sarah: Dump of mapping (head_id -> base_index range):
  - gemma: head0:[0..63], head1:[64..127], head2:[128..191]...
  - nova-lite converted: head0:[64..127], head1:[0..63], head2:[128..191]  <-- head0/1 swapped during reshape step in convert script

anya: Aha. That swap would explain token-position-dependent corruption. Looks like reshape ordering in the converter assumed Fortran vs C order when splitting heads.

kevin: If that's the case, a quick patch in the converter to use reshape(order='C') or explicit reshape + transpose should fix it. I can push a small PR. :+1:

sarah: I've opened a branch with a hacky fix (preserve_head_order). After re-conversion + int4 we see: ppl 13.8, rouge-L 0.39, main regression down to noise on our samples.

raj: Nice. Next steps: add a unit test to the onboarding pipeline that compares headwise rotary offsets and tokenization round-trip across model formats. And add the --preserve-rotary-order as a default for Gemma->Nova conversions until we have a better detection heuristic.

matt: Also add a small eval that runs a few prompts through float32 converted model vs quantized to catch semantic drops early. Save the eval prompts in the model's onboarding dir.

sarah: Will do. I put the reproducer + conversion diff in PR #3124 and added the failing example under examples/onboard/sentence-reorder.txt.

ci-bot: CI: tests/unit/rotary_mapping_test.py added, local pass.

sarah: Thanks all. Filing a follow-up to track downstream Dedicated/Hosted performance sanity after we roll the converter fix. :rocket:
